runs.text:
The Millbrook Hollow City Council met on Tuesday night. The council voted to approve a changed version of the parks and recreation line item. The meeting also covered the long-delayed replacement of the Third Street bridge.

A spokesperson for the mayor's office spoke about the revised figure. The spokesperson said the figure reflects "ongoing conversations" among council members. The spokesperson did not describe these conversations further.

Two council staffers linked a separate memo to the finance subcommittee. The memo set the adjustment at about $340,000. A budget analyst reviewed the memo. The analyst said the figure was "in the range we expected."

The memo contained another item near its end. No council member raised this item during the meeting. The item stated that the bridge's lead structural engineer had found a load-bearing crack. The engineer said the crack was serious. The engineer recommended closing the bridge to truck traffic within 90 days.

The bridge project has appeared on the capital plan since at least 2019. The project has already received 14 change orders. The council did not discuss the project in detail.

A reporter reached council member Dana Okafor after the meeting. Okafor said, "The process worked the way it's supposed to work, and I think residents should feel good about that."
